items.summary: YC startup Rivet launched on Hacker News on Nov 5 and officially on Nov 6: an open-source orchestrator where each agent runs as a long-lived, lightweight actor (claimed 4.99 ms p99 cold starts, 72 KB memory per actor), with state in per-actor SQLite backed by S3 and full self-hosting. Positioned as an alternative to Cloudflare Durable Objects and heavyweight per-agent sandboxes; 6,700+ stars at launch, with SDKs for TypeScript, Rust, Python and Swift.
items.title: Rivet: open-source actor orchestrator for agent workloads — lightweight durable actors instead of heavy sandboxes (launched Nov 6, Apache 2.0)

items.summary: Launched on Product Hunt on Oct 31, agentmash is an open-source shared-context layer for coding agents: every agent sees which files a teammate's agent is changing, and gets warned before editing a file a teammate's agent just touched, so parallel agents don't overwrite each other. It supports Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and 16+ agents, works with existing subscriptions, can be self-hosted, and ships a crew of 22 ready-made agents for planning, backend, tests, review and more.
items.title: agentmash: open-source multiplayer layer for teams' coding agents — agents stop overwriting each other's work (launched Oct 31)

items.summary: Released today, Nov 7, Select 1.0.0 is an open-source, self-hosted platform for managing teams of AI agents (Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL), with multi-agent teams, roles and task management. The author notes native Gmail/Microsoft 365 OAuth and sandboxed Claude Code/Codex execution are not in this release yet — this is the self-hosted core.
items.title: Select 1.0: open-source, self-hosted platform for managing teams of AI agents, with roles and task tracking (v1.0.0 released Nov 7)
